validity.researcher_notes: wiki_citations.json is empty for this row (this run's gem.wiki harvest is failing with Cloudflare 403 to automated fetch across the whole scope) and every ref unit in worklist.json for P4181 is class=MISSING_REF (Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Length, Diameter, Location, Owner) -- there is no existing sheet-cited source to re-verify; this is cold research. I attempted the row's own wiki URL directly (WebFetch) and it also 403'd, so I could not even read GEM's own citations for leads. Open-web search (DuckDuckGo html + Bing, English and Urdu) for the exact name 'Sakhakot-Swat Gas Pipeline' / 'Sakhakot' + 'Swat' + 'gas pipeline' returns ONLY the gem.wiki page and its scrapers/mirrors -- no independent source uses this pipeline's name, which on its own would be a hallmark existence flag. However, I did find real, independent, non-GEM evidence that SNGPL operates gas transmission infrastructure in exactly this corridor and of a matching caliber: (1) Zameen.com news (27 May 2020) reporting SNGPL's plan, announced by the Federal Minister of Energy and KP Chief Minister, to lay an EIGHT-INCH gas pipeline to fix chronic low winter gas pressure in Mingora and Saidu Sharif, Swat district -- diameter matches GEM's recorded 8in for this row, though the article never says 'Sakhakot' or states a 68.06 km length, so it corroborates the general phenomenon (an 8in SNGPL line feeding Swat) but not this specific named/measured segment; (2) a 2020s Urdu-language item (Facebook/Swat Voice) describes a separate 12-inch pipeline laid for the same Mingora low-pressure problem under KP CM Mahmood Khan -- a DIFFERENT diameter, showing Swat's gas network has more than one line of different calibers, so diameter alone is not a safe match signal; (3) Dawn.com (2026, https://www.dawn.com/news/1753232) confirms SNGPL is indeed the utility billing/operating gas service inside Swat proper (a meter-rent legal dispute) -- supports the Owner=SNGPL attribution being at least plausible, not GEM-only, but again doesn't name this segment; (4) SNGPL's own official 2006 annual-report transmission-system map (sngpl.com.pk/download/AR2006/MAP.pdf) labels 'Sakhakot' as a place within the NWFP network region, but the map has no text layer (pdftotext returns nothing) and at the rendered resolution I could not make out a distinct drawn pipeline reaching it separately from the Peshawar/Mardan/Swabi trunk cluster -- inconclusive, and 20 years stale regardless. NET: SNGPL gas infrastructure genuinely reaches Swat district via the Mardan/Malakand corridor and includes at least one project of matching 8-inch caliber, so this is not a pure fabrication -- but no source independently corroborates THIS exact named segment (start=Sakhakot, 68.06 km) to the standing >=2-independent-source bar. Flagging as an existence/verification concern rather than confirmed.

validity.researcher_notes: Three roster rows all converge on the same Nowshera-Mardan-Malakand-Swat corridor: P4179 runs Nowshera->...->Sakhakot (57.99 km, 8in), P4181 (this row) runs Sakhakot->Swat (68.06 km, 8in), and P5486 is separately named 'Mardan-Swat Gas Pipeline' with a recorded StartLocation of Nowshera (104.89 km, 12in) -- i.e. a third row nominally covering the same Nowshera-to-Swat routing under a different name/segmentation. The two routings do not reconcile arithmetically: P4179+P4181 = 126.05 km end-to-end vs P5486's 104.89 km for what its name implies is a similar Nowshera/Mardan-to-Swat run, and the diameters differ (8in+8in vs 12in). This is consistent with either (a) three genuinely distinct pipes/loop-lines built in different eras of SNGPL's decades-old network (plausible and common in this dataset), or (b) an overlapping/duplicated record where P5486 double-counts ground that P4179+P4181 already cover under a different name. I could not resolve this from open-web sources (none name any of these three lines specifically) -- this needs a route-geometry or internal SNGPL-map check, which is outside this row's ref-verification scope but worth flagging given the scope note's emphasis on duplicate-hunting in this corridor.

summary: P4181 (Sakhakot-Swat Gas Pipeline): existence concern -- no independent source names this exact segment (gem.wiki 403'd, only GEM mirrors found by name), though SNGPL is independently confirmed to run an 8-inch gas line into Swat district (Zameen 2020) and to operate in Swat generally (Dawn); also flagged a duplicate/overlap concern vs P5486 (Mardan-Swat, 12in) + P4179 (Nowshera-...-Sakhakot) whose lengths don't reconcile. No fields could be responsibly filled with a verified ref this pass; all proposed items are low-tier circumstantial leads, not confirmations.
